settlementFee.note: PENNSYLVANIA IS A RATING-BUREAU-UNIFORM, ALL-INCLUSIVE-RATE STATE: TIRBOP's Manual, filed with and approved by the PA Insurance Department under The Insurance Company Law of 1921 (40 P.S. section 910-41), sets a single 'Charge' that under the COMPANY OR AGENT PROCEDURE legally BUNDLES the title insurance premium together with title search, examination, escrow, and settlement/closing services into ONE all-inclusive rate (Section 1.6: 'Charge(s) ... includes premium, examination and settlement or closing fee and every other Charge'). This is the regulatory backbone -- not a provider-set price -- and is the same byte-for-byte across every TIRBOP member/agent in the state. HOWEVER, TIRBOP's Manual also creates the exact structural carve-out the task brief anticipated: under the ALTERNATIVE 'APPROVED ATTORNEY PROCEDURE' (Section 5.1.B), the Approved Attorney -- not the Insurer/Agent -- personally certifies title and conducts settlement, and Section 5.1.C states in so many words: 'The charge for the search, examination of title and the settlement by the Approved Attorney is NOT governed by this Manual.' That attorney-side settlement charge is therefore entirely unregulated and left to the individual attorney/market, exactly matching this survey's target. TIRBOP additionally lists, in Section 2.1(a)-(e), five specific categories explicitly EXCLUDED from even the all-inclusive Company/Agent rate and therefore separately, unregulated-ly chargeable by ANY provider type: (a) document preparation other than the commitment/closing statement/policy, (b) government recording charges, (c) overnight delivery, (d) bank wire transfer, and (e) receipt/printing of electronically-transmitted documents other than the commitment/closing statement/policy -- i.e., doc prep, courier/overnight, and wire fees are NOT part of the regulated rate anywhere in Pennsylvania, confirming the brief's framing that these service-fee categories vary by provider even though the core premium does not.
settlementFee.saleRateTable_representativeTiers: Company/Agent Procedure, Sale Rate (owner's policies): $0-$30,000 = $569.00 flat; add $7.41/thousand from $30,001-$45,000; $6.27/thousand from $45,001-$100,000 (so $100,000 total = $1,025.00); $5.70/thousand from $100,001-$500,000 (so $200,000 = $1,595.00; $500,000 = $2,850.00 -- reconstructed from the per-tier formula); $4.56/thousand from $500,001-$1,000,000 (so $1,000,000 = $5,130.00); further tiers to $30,000,000+.
settlementFee.nonSaleRateTable_representativeTiers: Company/Agent Procedure, Non-Sale Rate (loan policies): $0-$30,000 = $512.00 flat; add $5.98/thousand from $30,001-$45,000; $5.41/thousand from $45,001-$100,000 (so $100,000 = $899.25); $4.84/thousand from $100,001-$500,000 (so $200,000 = $1,383.25); $4.27/thousand from $500,001-$1,000,000; further tiers to $30,000,000+.
settlementFee.approvedAttorneyRateTable_representative: Approved Attorney Procedure (Section 5.51): $0-$30,000 = $142.00 flat; add $3.70/thousand from $30,001-$100,000 (so $100,000 = $401.00 -- Manual's own worked example shows $200,000 = $714.00); add $3.13/thousand from $100,001-$500,000; add $2.85/thousand from $500,001-$1,000,000; further tiers to $7,000,000+. NOTE: the Approved Attorney Rate is dramatically lower than the Company/Agent Sale Rate at every tier (e.g., $200,000: $714.00 Approved Attorney vs. $1,595.00 Company/Agent Sale Rate) precisely BECAUSE it excludes the settlement/search/exam work the Approved Attorney performs and bills separately, unregulated, per Section 5.1.C -- the rate differential is the clearest quantitative proof in this survey of how much of the 'all-inclusive' Company/Agent charge is actually attributable to settlement services.

bundlingNotes: PA's TIRBOP structure is the single clearest illustration in this survey of the task brief's core distinction: the Company/Agent Procedure's 'all-inclusive' Sale/Non-Sale Rate is rating-bureau-uniform and covers premium + search + exam + escrow + settlement as ONE regulated Charge (confirmed identical across the 04/01/23 and 08/01/24 manual vintages, and independently cross-verified against a 2019-vintage Old Republic Title/Carbon Search and Settlement Services Inc. republication of the same Sale/Non-Sale table at https://cdn.hibuwebsites.com/f29812e7658842deae54ba229abe69a8/files/uploaded/Carbon-Search-And-Settlement-Services-Inc-Title-Insurance-Rates.pdf -- byte-for-byte identical base rates back to at least August 2019, meaning the TIRBOP rate table has been stable for 5+ years). But TIRBOP itself creates two distinct escape hatches from that bundling: (1) the Approved Attorney Procedure, where the attorney's own search/exam/settlement charge is expressly NOT governed by the Manual at all (Section 5.1.C) -- and PA's real-world mix of title-agent-run and attorney-run closings (the 'table funding'/attorney-involvement-varies pattern flagged in the task brief) means a meaningful share of PA closings are priced this way; and (2) Section 2.1(a)-(e)'s carve-outs for doc prep, recording, overnight delivery, wire transfer, and e-doc printing, which apply to EVERY provider type regardless of procedure and are the primary channel through which PA providers actually compete on price even under the Company/Agent Procedure.
transactionContext: Applies uniformly to Owner's and Loan policy premiums statewide, all counties, all provider types that are TIRBOP members/agents. No purchase-vs-refinance rate distinction (rate depends only on liability/loan amount, and on which of the two Procedures -- Company/Agent vs. Approved Attorney -- is used for a given transaction).
